To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the pedagogies of the art practices we studied were immanent to the art works and events; (b) the force and affect of art practices were individuating, and (c) these individuations were virtual and transcendent, and as such, exceeded the actualities of the art practices and events.
art practices can be used to explore the idea that learning is a force of individuation and that this can have implications for pedagogical practices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the individuation of learning and with the individuation and individuation of the subject.
the question of what is the force of art in the domain of pedagogy.
the question of how to think and act in the face of an uncertain future, and the ways in which art and pedagogy might contribute to a re-thinking of the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the force of art is to individuate new forms of thought, knowledge and being, to open new worlds, to create new possibilities of being and becoming.
the event of art is a pedagogical force in the individuation of a subject-yot-come.
learning is a force of individuation, and the individuation of a new world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
art, pedagogies and becomings are all about the force of art and the individuation of new worlds.
the subject is not yet born, and that the task of art and pedagogies of art is to help to individuate the subject-to-come.
the subject is not a subject, but a subject-yet to come, which is not a subject at all, but the subject of an event.
The main takeaway from our work is that

learning is not a process in which a learner acquires knowledge or a set of skills, but is rather a process of becoming, a process of individuation, in which a learner comes to be in relation with others, with the world, and with knowledge.
learning is a process of individuation, which is not only the becoming-other of the learner but also the becoming-other of knowledge itself, which is always in the process of being actualized.
the pedagogical event is not a matter of a teacher, a learner, and a knowledge to be transmitted.
